title: Appendix C — Motives and Motifs in the Poetry of Marianne Moore
folder: Burke - Motives and Motifs in Marianne Moore
agent_role: single-agent full-unit Phase 2 deep-analysis; oeuvre-level dramatism worked example

outline.topic: Moore's poetic strategy as relation between visible/invisible, external/internal; against Symbolist, Imagist, Objectivist labels; objects studied 'in their own right' once subjectively selected; the four quartz clocks as objectivist exhibit; act/scene/agent named openly as 'three terms central to the philosophy of drama embodied in Henry James's prefaces'; appreciation as motive; 'Spenser's Ireland' read as covert lyric whose preceding description is scene-context to a final assertive act

What are Years? as titular thesaurus question; years as quality of observation, courage, mortality, captivity-affirmation; comparison of 'Sojourn in the Whale' (oppositional rising water) with the affirmative captive bird singing; ostracizing-of-the-enemy as feminine refutational tactic vs. eristic dialectic; the synecdochic reversibility of motifs (chasm in sea ↔ sea in chasm; container/contained interchangeable); 'years' subsume synecdoche; 'years are poetry'

Substantiality of motifs: 'all branches spread from a single trunk'; surfaces derived from depth; objects have property not of things but of volitions; 'Black Earth' as rare 'I' poem identifying poet with elephant; reading the later 'Smooth Gnarled Crape Myrtle' trunk-image through the earlier 'Black Earth' as access to 'realism in its purity'; word as collapsed history, narrative implicit in simultaneity; 'To a Snail' equating compression-style with moral contractility

Contractility as jeopardy and coquetry; butterfly poem with two moments of stasis (nymph-confrontation and zephyr-colloquy); the 'menagerie almost a thesaurus of protectivenesses' (Pangolin, armored animal); cult of rarity and word-play as tonal contractility; closing poem 'The Paper Nautilus' merging bondage/freedom and poet-poem ↔ mother-young attachment

concepts.name: oeuvre-level dramatism
concepts.description: Reading an author's complete body of work — not a single poem — as a dramatistic-analytic object. The pentad is applied to the *strategy* visible only across many texts, where recurrent motifs disclose a stable underlying motive-structure.

concepts.name: poetic strategy as substance
concepts.description: Burke proposes to 'characterize the substance of Miss Moore's work as a specific poetic strategy.' Substance here is not metaphysical essence but the configuration of recurrent motivational choices an author repeatedly makes.

concepts.name: visible/invisible relation
concepts.description: The defining axis of Moore's poems: a relation between external and internal, visible and invisible, background and personality. Moore's 'observations' are visions whose objects retain their own right.

concepts.name: symbolism / imagism / objectivism (the proportion theory)
concepts.description: Three idioms with the same ingredients in different proportions: symbolism features subject-over-object; imagism balances them; objectivism, having selected an object for subjective reasons, then studies it in its own right.

concepts.name: objectivist reporting that is not journalism
concepts.description: Moore's descriptive verse reports objects but is not reportage; the object is studied for itself yet betrays its motivated selection.

concepts.name: withinness-of-withinness / motives-behind-motives
concepts.description: Moore's strategy figures not merely interior motive but the motive of motive — exemplified by clocks that tell time to clocks that tell time.

concepts.name: appreciation as motive (Jamesian)
concepts.description: Burke explicitly invokes Henry James's *Spoils of Poynton* preface: appreciation as the form of gratitude that 'redeems' complaint. Appreciation is the closest secular equivalent to glorification.

concepts.name: scene–act ratio as compositional logic of a descriptive lyric
concepts.description: In 'Spenser's Ireland' the descriptive material is read as scene/background that contains the same quality as the final assertive act ('I am Irish, dissatisfied'). Burke makes the scene–act ratio do compositional work.

concepts.name: because → and substitution
concepts.description: Moore's objectivist idiom rewrites lyric causation as conjunction: where the lyrist says 'I am sad because…' Moore says 'such-and-such — and I am sad.' The scene becomes objective replica of the subjective.

concepts.name: ostracizing the enemy / refutation by silence
concepts.description: Moore's characteristic non-eristic dialectical posture: she does not dispute her opponent but excludes him from attention. Burke frames this as a feminine alternative to dialectic-as-disputation.

concepts.name: synecdochic reversibility (container ↔ contained)
concepts.description: 'A chasm in the sea becomes rather the sea in a chasm.' Years subsume the synecdochic capacities by which elements that cluster together can represent each other; active/passive and environed/environment are interchangeable.

concepts.name: substantiality of motifs (single trunk)
concepts.description: The motifs of a genuine poetry are not assembled like planks; they branch from a single trunk. Surfaces derive from depth; lawful selection of surfaces *is* depth.

concepts.name: objects as volitions
concepts.description: In Moore's verse the objects treated have the property not simply of things but of volitions; they derive poignancy from their relation to the sources of motive. Object ↔ act collapse.

concepts.name: conversities
concepts.description: Moore's own term, adopted by Burke for the observer–observed relation in her verse: not news/reporter, but conversities — mutual address between mind and thing.

concepts.name: trunk-as-act (Black Earth ↔ Crape Myrtle)
concepts.description: Reading the later condensed image of the elephant's trunk through the earlier 'Black Earth' identification recovers volitional sediment behind a surface thing-perception: 'a glimpse of realism in its purity.'

concepts.name: word as collapsed history
concepts.description: Within a chosen word a sequence is implicit — 'a complexity of possible narratives that could be drawn from it.' Sensitivity in word-choice = ability to feel a future history behind the word.

concepts.name: contractility (style ↔ virtue)
concepts.description: In 'To a Snail,' compression-as-style and contractility-as-virtue are equated; the principle of style is located in the occipital horn. Esthetic value and moral value share substance.

concepts.name: jeopardy
concepts.description: The mood of tentativeness, contractility under threat; the fastidious creatures of Moore's menagerie ('almost a thesaurus of protectivenesses') figure jeopardy as Moore's recurrent motivational scene.

concepts.name: two moments of stasis (butterfly poem)
concepts.description: Burke reads the butterfly poem as figuring two motivational levels: a first stasis (elf ↔ nymph confrontation) and a second (butterfly ↔ zephyr colloquy) that occupies the 'motives-behind-motives' deity-level.

concepts.name: oeuvre as cross-poem context
concepts.description: A usage in any given poem is finished, but becomes 'work in progress' when aligned with kindred usages across the oeuvre. The oeuvre is the unit of motivational legibility.

concepts.name: armored animals / protectivenesses thesaurus
concepts.description: Moore's pangolin, jerboa, elephant, snail, paper nautilus, fish all figure protective contractility — a recurring motif Burke reads as a single motivational signature.

concepts.name: bondage/freedom merger (Paper Nautilus)
concepts.description: The closing poem of *What Are Years* merges bondage and freedom ('hindered to succeed') in the maternal attachment of poet to poem.

oeuvre_level_dramatism.definition: Dramatistic analysis whose analytic object is an author's complete published body of work treated as a single substance-bearing strategy, rather than any single text.
core_moves: Identify recurring motifs (Moore: visibles, animals, armor, contractility, water-in-imprisonment, clocks-for-clocks) and treat their convergence as evidence of an underlying motive-structure.

Read each individual text's surface against the cross-textual sediment: a thing in poem-B becomes legible as an act when poem-A has previously charged the same image with volition (Crape Myrtle trunk ↔ Black Earth elephant).

Detect the dominant pentad ratio across the oeuvre — for Moore, act–agent (Moore's signature attentive act expresses her agent-character) and scene–act (descriptive scene is logical ground of the assertive act).
Diagnose the proportion of symbolist/imagist/objectivist ingredients the strategy actually mixes, rather than accepting any single label.
Use one author-internal essay (here, *Spenser's Ireland*, *To a Snail*, *Black Earth*) as exegetical key to the rest of the corpus.
Treat methodological poems (Moore's pre-1935 'Poetry,' 'Critics and Connoisseurs,' etc.) as native ars poetica that the analyst leverages rather than overrides.
oeuvre_level_dramatism.contrast_with_keats_appendix: GM-10 (Keats) works a single ode; GM-12 works a whole oeuvre. The Keats appendix uses dense intra-textual ratio analysis; the Moore appendix uses cross-textual motif tracking and oeuvre-level substantiality — 'all branches spread from a single trunk.' Moore appendix is the *scale-shift* template: from single-text dramatism to corpus-scale dramatism.

featured_terms.role: Moore's signature *act* is the attentive descriptive observation. Burke names act/scene/agent at book p. 489 as the three terms structurally at work in her poetry. 'Trunk as act' (book p. 498) is the chapter's strongest pentad-statement: the thing-perceived becomes an act-perceived when its volitional charge is recovered.

Moore's descriptive material functions as scene/background that *contains the same quality* as the final assertive act. The scene–act ratio is the compositional engine of poems Burke reads as covert lyrics (Spenser's Ireland).

Moore-as-poet and the scene-internal agents (animals, the Irish girl, the elephant, the unicorn, the basilisk) are paired through the appropriate-scene-to-agent ratio. The 'I' of 'Black Earth' is a rare overt agent-identification with elephant-as-scene-internal-agent.

absent_or_recessive_terms.role: Almost wholly recessive: Moore is not concerned with means-to-ends; she is concerned with object-attention and motivational substance.

Present only in the appreciation-as-motive subroutine (book p. 489) and at the deity-level of the butterfly footnote (book pp. 499-500). Burke treats Moore's appreciation as the secular analog of mystical glorification, but does not feature Purpose.

featured_ratios.description: The attentive act expresses the agent-character. Moore's verses are diagnostic of Moore-as-agent because the act of attention is signature.
Description (scene) is read as logical-compositional ground of the assertive act it brackets ('Spenser's Ireland').
Catalogue of correspondences between agents and their appropriate scenes ('People's Surroundings'); the basilisk lives in a basilica.

methodological_template_for_dissertation.core_claim: GM-12 is the dissertation's template for applying dramatism at *corpus scale* — a player's body of play across games, a game-studio's body of releases, a designer's career, a player-community's archive — by reading recurrent motifs across the corpus as evidence of a stable motivational substance.

transfer_steps.name: Choose corpus boundary
transfer_steps.moore_analog: Burke uses *Selected Poems* (1935) + *What Are Years* (1941); admits an *Observations* (1924) backstop.
transfer_steps.dissertation_analog: Choose the unit: a player's recorded sessions across N games; a studio's released titles; a community's forum/wiki archive; a designer's portfolio.

transfer_steps.name: Catalog recurrent motifs
transfer_steps.moore_analog: Armored animals, visibles/invisibles, water-in-imprisonment, clocks-for-clocks, contractility, jeopardy.
transfer_steps.dissertation_analog: Recurrent game-design choices (mechanics, level-archetypes, character-tropes); recurrent player-behaviors (build-types, route patterns, social-stances); recurrent community discourse-moves.

transfer_steps.name: Identify the underlying motivational substance
transfer_steps.moore_analog: Burke names appreciation, contractility, jeopardy, withinness-of-withinness as the substance-structure.
transfer_steps.dissertation_analog: Name the strategy: e.g., 'this player-community's substance is mastery-display-through-self-imposed-constraint'; 'this studio's substance is environmental-storytelling-as-act'; 'this designer's substance is agency-restoration-after-loss.'

transfer_steps.name: Diagnose featured pentad term(s)
transfer_steps.dissertation_analog: Calleja-PIM correspondences: a corpus featuring 'kinesthetic involvement' features Agency; one featuring 'narrative involvement' features Scene+Purpose; one featuring 'shared involvement' features Agent. The pentad-feature diagnosis IS the corpus-strategy.

transfer_steps.name: Use one internal exhibit as exegetical key
transfer_steps.moore_analog: Black Earth → Crape Myrtle: a prior overt usage decodes a later condensed one.
transfer_steps.dissertation_analog: Choose one paradigmatic player-trace / community-event / design-document and read the rest of the corpus through it.

transfer_steps.name: Test the substance against cross-motif convergence
transfer_steps.moore_analog: 'All branches spread from a single trunk' — if the motifs do not converge on a single substance, the analysis is wrong.
transfer_steps.dissertation_analog: Refutation condition: if recurrent motifs do not coherently express the proposed substance, the proposed motivational diagnosis fails.

transfer_steps.name: Read individual artifacts as 'work in progress' within the corpus
transfer_steps.moore_analog: 'A usage … becomes in effect work in progress when we align it with kindred usages.'
transfer_steps.dissertation_analog: No single play-session, no single design-document, no single forum-post is final; each is legible only against cross-corpus sediment.

what_this_template_avoids: Reduction of player/designer/community analysis to a single 'representative' artifact (the single-poem mistake).
Treatment of motifs as planks rather than branches (additive cataloging without substance-identification).
Conflation of label (symbolist, imagist, objectivist; ludologist, narratologist, etc.) with strategy (the actual proportions of ingredients).

positions.claim: Moore's poetic substance is a specific strategy, recoverable across her oeuvre as the recurrent configuration of attentive-act, descriptive-scene, and appreciative-agent.
positions.evidence: Burke's opening commitment + the cross-poem motif-tracking that follows.

positions.claim: Moore is mis-classified as Symbolist, Imagist, or Objectivist taken singly; her strategy mixes the ingredients of all three in distinctive proportion, with objectivist features dominant but subjective motivation conditioning selection.
positions.evidence: The electrician analogy + 'Four Quartz Crystal Clocks' reading + the 'objectivist' qualification 'only by taking away the epithet in part.'

positions.claim: Appreciation functions as a primary motive in Moore's verse and is the secular equivalent of religious glorification; it is the redemptive operation that converts complaint into precision.
positions.evidence: Burke's explicit invocation of Henry James's *Spoils of Poynton* preface and the reading of 'Spenser's Ireland.'

positions.claim: Moore's motifs (armored animals, water-in-imprisonment, contractility) are substantially unified — branches from a single trunk — and the unifying substance is a strategy of attentive-protectiveness under jeopardy.
positions.anchor: book p. 496 (substantiality) + book p. 500 (thesaurus of protectivenesses)
positions.evidence: Burke's cross-poem motif-convergence argument + the *Pangolin* 'another armoured animal' opening as diagnostic moment.

positions.claim: Oeuvre-level dramatism is methodologically distinct from single-text dramatism: the unit of motivational legibility is the corpus, not the poem. A condensed image (Crape Myrtle trunk) is legible as act only against an earlier overt usage (Black Earth elephant).
positions.evidence: 'A usage … becomes in effect work in progress when we align it with kindred usages.'

positions.claim: In Moore's verse the object/thing distinction collapses into object/act: objects 'have the property not simply of things but of volitions.' This is the strongest moment of realism in the volume.
positions.evidence: 'A glimpse of realism in its purity'; 'conversities.'

tensions.name: objectivist vs. motivated-selection
tensions.description: Moore's verse looks descriptively objectivist but the cross-poem pattern reveals a strict principle of selection; Burke calls her 'objectivist only by taking away the epithet in part.' The tension is between the surface objectivist appearance and the deeper symbolist motivation.

tensions.name: single-poem finish vs. oeuvre work-in-progress
tensions.description: Each finished poem is 'brilliant with surface,' yet becomes 'work in progress' once aligned with kindred usages. A poem is simultaneously complete and provisional. The tension is methodological: the unit of analysis is the poem, but the unit of legibility is the oeuvre.

tensions.name: contractility as virtue vs. as jeopardy
tensions.description: Contractility (snail occipital horn, armored pangolin) is at once a positive esthetic-moral virtue (compression-as-style) and a defensive posture under threat (jeopardy, fledglings + stalking cat). The single substance polarizes into affirmation and vulnerability.

tensions.name: scene-act-agent featured / agency-purpose recessive
tensions.description: Only three of five pentad terms structure Moore's oeuvre per Burke's reading. The recessive Agency-Purpose pair is itself diagnostic: Moore's poetry refuses the means/ends idiom of pragmatism and the teleology of mysticism (despite the secular-glorification analog).
tensions.page_locus: implicit throughout; explicit at book p. 489 for the three featured

cross_pipeline_bridges.anchor: PIM (Player Involvement Model) is a six-dimensional player-involvement taxonomy. The oeuvre-level dramatism template applies natively: a player-corpus is read for recurrent PIM-dimension featuring (kinesthetic / spatial / shared / narrative / affective / ludic). Moore's appendix is the methodological precedent for treating a player or community as a substance-bearing strategy.

Moore's object-as-volition resonates with Aristotle's energeia/dynamis as Heidegger reads them: the thing as actuality, not the thing as stuff. Burke's 'realism in its purity' moment (Crape Myrtle trunk through Black Earth) parallels Heidegger's claim that Being is read in act, not in substance-as-stuff.

Moore's visible/invisible relation (the visible's power is the invisible) provides a poetic analog to phantasia as image-presentation that opens onto the noetic. The 'scene–agent' fittingness (basilisk in basilica) tracks Aristotelian to-prepon.

Moore's animals each have an appropriate scene (jerboa honors sand by assuming its color); each is figured in its own Umwelt. The chapter's menagerie-as-thesaurus-of-protectivenesses runs through bio-rhetorical lines that converge with Uexküll's species-specific perceptual worlds.
Moore's descriptive scene that 'contains the same quality as the act' is a Burkean prefiguration of Rickert's ambient agency: scene is not background but co-actant.
Moore's redemption of complaint into precision parallels Gross's incipient-act framework: emotion arrested at the threshold of action and transformed in the holding.
The appreciation-as-motive routine prefigures consubstantiation/identification: Moore's appropriation of the object 'as one's own' is a substance-sharing claim awaiting the 1950 vocabulary.
GM-10 single-text dramatism + GM-12 oeuvre-dramatism = paired methodological appendices establishing two scales of dramatistic-analytic application.
Moore's synecdochic reversibility (chasm-in-sea ↔ sea-in-chasm; active ↔ passive; container ↔ contained) is a worked instance of the synecdoche trope GM-13 will theorize.
